product.schneider-pc1640.summary: The PC1512 successor that brought EGA graphics to Schneider’s Topline range.
product.schneider-pc1640.history: In July 1987, Schneider announced Amstrad’s PC1640 in its Topline range for medium-sized and large businesses. Computerwoche quoted about DM 2,700 with one floppy drive and an EGA monitor.
product.schneider-pc1640.technical.limit: A BIOS attributed to a Schneider unit is needed for comparison with Amstrad’s firmware and validation in BluMach. A photograph of the Schneider model with clear reuse rights is also pending.
product.schneider-pc1640.technical.sourc: Heinz Nixdorf MuseumsForum, Das war der Schneider Euro PC, 09-05-2023
product.schneider-pc1640.technical.detai: The monitor determined which graphics modes were available. The German manual documents the PC-ECD for 640 × 350 EGA in 16 colours from a palette of 64.
product.schneider-pc1640.technical.perio: Computerwoche · PC 1640 soll bei Großkunden ankommen · 07/1987
